provenanceNote: Finland and Norway do not collide, and this is the pair where the near-miss is purely a matter of what counts as a character. Both are eleven characters long. Norway's are eleven *digits*; a Finnish code's seventh is always a non-digit marker and its eleventh may be a letter. So no string satisfies both, and detect() reports exactly one scheme. allowSyntheticNumbers is opted in deliberately even though this value is Finnish: it proves the absence holds under the most permissive options a caller can pass, rather than only under the defaults that would refuse every constructible Norwegian value anyway. Published by DVV on Suomi.fi for Service Developers and vendored at spec/sources/dvv/test-identities.csv. Individual number 952, inside the 900-999 block DVV states it does not issue from, so the code is entered in no population register and identifies nobody. CLAUDE.md's Exception 3.

The other direction of the same pair, which is why both are here: an all-digit eleven-character value is Norwegian and cannot be Finnish, because position seven must be a marker. Month 91 (11 + 80) is Skatteetaten's synthetic-test convention -- not a calendar month, so no bearer can exist. generated.csv's fnr-499-000 row, individual 250. CLAUDE.md's Exception 1.
